content:
Rapper Macklemore has been dropped from the remaining dates of Ed Sheeran's US Loop Tour following his "Free Palestine" remarks at the start of the month during Sheeran's US concert run.

Messina Touring Group, the promoter of Ed Sheeran's US Loop Tour, told Rolling Stone in a statement: "As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran's US Loop Tour, we were informed that the promoters of the upcoming US tour venues made it clear that Macklemore would not be allowed to continue performing on the concert lineup, otherwise the entire tour would be cancelled, affecting hundreds of thousands of fans. After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will no longer be participating in the remaining support slots."

On September 4, the "Thrift Shop" rapper shared his long publicly expressed pro-Palestinian stance with thousands of concertgoers at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.

In concert footage (posted to his Instagram account), Macklemore said: "One of the reasons I wanted to be part of this tour was so I could say two words that mean so much to me on stages and in stadiums all across America: Free Palestine. I said 'Free Palestine'. I hope those words are heard loud and clear, so that the people from Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them."

Although Macklemore's remarks drew cheers from many in the audience, some concertgoers were reportedly seen leaving during his set.

Macklemore's concert remarks gained wider attention after singer Pink reposted a post from StopAntisemitism. The post criticised Macklemore's comments as "anti-Israel propaganda", claimed he "falsely accused Israel of genocide" and demanded refunds for Jewish concertgoers. Notably, StopAntisemitism has long been accused of harassing and doxxing those who publicly criticise Israel.

Following the backlash from fans, Pink attempted to clarify on Instagram why she had shared the StopAntisemitism post, acknowledging that while the post "used some wording that I would not have used, and not every word I would have chosen", she believed that "Palestinians deserve a future that honours their humanity and aspirations", and stated that "Hamas is a terrorist organisation".

Pink wrote: "Protecting innocent lives always comes first, everywhere, and no one should be celebrating the death of any child, any child." She added: "I have been a UNICEF ambassador for ten years, caring for children who have no say in the country or war they were born into, and I mourn every single one of them, on either side of the fence."

On Monday, Macklemore posted a lengthy statement on Instagram responding to his removal from Sheeran's tour. In the statement, he appeared to blame his firing on a specific figure — one who is not Pink or Sheeran.

He instead accused New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium owner Robert Kraft of lobbying other stadium owners to refuse Macklemore from performing at their venues.

Macklemore wrote: "Last Monday, while the media focus was on Pink and I and what was said at MetLife, Ed told me that Robert Kraft had called him. We were scheduled to play Gillette Stadium later this month, which is owned by the Kraft Group. Ed told me Kraft said I was not allowed to perform at his stadium. Ed also told me Kraft had contacted several other stadium owners, and they had given him an ultimatum: if Macklemore stays on the tour, you can't play at our venues."

Macklemore also said he had "had a few difficult conversations with Sheeran over the past couple of weeks" and expressed some disappointment in the singer.

Macklemore wrote: "Ed is in a really f***ing difficult position, and he knows it. His longstanding stance of not being political is being challenged like never before. He said the words 'Free Palestine' and the image of the Palestinian flag have hurt a lot of people he has come across. I told him that if those words are more offensive than the tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there's a fundamental disconnect between those people and me. But he couldn't get past his own public-facing 'I don't take sides' threshold."

Kraft told the outlet: "Gillette Stadium has always been committed to providing a welcoming environment for all visitors and ensuring that events held at our venue do not become a platform for hate speech."

He added: "Over the past decade, most of my time and energy has been focused on combating antisemitism and hate in all its forms, and when I felt that line had been crossed, I felt it was my responsibility to speak up."
